title: Practice: Effect of Catalysts on Rate

questions.stem: A student adds manganese dioxide to hydrogen peroxide solution. Bubbling occurs rapidly. After the reaction, she filters the mixture and weighs the manganese dioxide. What would she find?

options.text: The mass has decreased because some was used up in the reaction
The mass has increased because oxygen was absorbed
The mass is unchanged because catalysts are not consumed in the reaction
The manganese dioxide has dissolved completely

questions.explanation: Catalysts speed up reactions without being used up. The manganese dioxide provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy for the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2) but is chemically unchanged at the end. The same mass of MnO2 would be recovered.

questions.stem: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction. In terms of activation energy and collision theory, how does it achieve this?

options.text: It increases the temperature of the reactants
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, so more collisions are successful
It increases the concentration of the reactants
It increases the energy of each collision

questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway that has a lower activation energy. This means that a greater proportion of collisions between reactant particles have sufficient energy to overcome this lower energy barrier. More successful collisions per second means a faster rate. The catalyst does not change temperature, concentration, or collision energy.

questions.stem: Enzymes are biological catalysts. Amylase catalyses the breakdown of starch but has no effect on protein digestion. What does this demonstrate about catalysts?

options.text: Catalysts only work at body temperature
Catalysts are specific - each catalyst works on particular reactions
Catalysts only work with biological molecules
Catalysts become used up after one reaction

questions.explanation: Catalysts are often specific to particular reactions. Amylase has an active site that fits starch molecules but not protein molecules. This specificity applies to industrial catalysts too - iron catalyses the Haber process but would not work for other reactions. Different reactions require different catalysts.

questions.stem: The Haber process uses an iron catalyst at 450°C. If the catalyst were not used, a much higher temperature would be needed to achieve a reasonable rate. Why is using a catalyst at a lower temperature economically beneficial?

options.text: Lower temperature produces more ammonia because the forward reaction is exothermic
Using a catalyst and lower temperature reduces energy costs while maintaining an acceptable rate
The catalyst is free, so it always saves money
Higher temperatures would destroy the ammonia produced

questions.explanation: Without a catalyst, a much higher temperature would be needed for a reasonable rate, which costs more energy (heating fuel). The iron catalyst allows the reaction to proceed at an acceptable rate at the lower temperature of 450°C, saving significant energy costs. Additionally, the lower temperature also favours a higher equilibrium yield of ammonia (since the forward reaction is exothermic).

questions.stem: A student plots two rate curves for the same reaction - one with a catalyst and one without. Both use identical amounts of reactants. How do the curves compare?

options.text: The catalysed reaction is steeper initially and reaches a higher final volume
The catalysed reaction is steeper initially but reaches the same final volume sooner
Both curves are identical because the catalyst does not change the amount of product
The catalysed reaction reaches a lower final volume because some reactant sticks to the catalyst

questions.explanation: The catalyst increases the rate (steeper initial curve) but does not change the total amount of product formed (same final volume of gas, since the same amounts of reactants are used). The catalysed reaction simply reaches completion sooner. The curve levels off at the same height but earlier in time.
